headline: Former UPSC Aspirant Hired As 'Professional Exam-Paper Protector' Claims He Has Been Guarding The Same Biology Question For Seven Years
body:
Q: Mr. Sharma, you have been stationed at this specific facility for seven years. Can you explain your daily routine as an official exam-paper bodyguard?

A: It is a high-stakes role. I don’t just watch the papers; I provide them with emotional support and tactical cover. Every morning at 6 AM, I verify the structural integrity of the ink, and by noon, I am essentially performing a rhythmic patrol around the safe, humming patriotic songs to ensure the exam questions remain optimistic and leak-proof.

Q: Is it true that the Supreme Court’s recent comments about moving exam administration to a more 'scientifically equipped body' have caused anxiety among your files?

A: Oh, the papers are terrified. They have grown quite attached to my particular brand of surveillance. If you move a document from a system that relies on a single man with a flashlight to a system that uses satellites and advanced encryption, the papers will suffer from culture shock. My wards are used to the 'human touch' of me checking if they’re cold every two hours.

Q: What will you do if the government officially transitions the entire process to a more efficient, automated framework?

A: I have already started drafting my resignation letter, though I suspect the ink will be too nervous to leave the page. I plan to open a boutique consultancy where I teach government files how to handle the trauma of being graded by a machine instead of a very tired, very dedicated civil servant.
caption: Job security is all about how hard you guard that one biology question. 📂👮‍♂️ #ExamSeason #UpscDiaries #NTA #GovernmentWork #JobSecurity (satire)
